ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A triangular piece of material is shown in the figure, where $ \angle A=30^\circ$, $ \angle C=90^\circ$, and $ AB=12$. A rectangle CDEF is cut from this material, with points D, E, and F located on AC, AB, and BC, respectively. Let the length of AE be $x$, and the area of rectangle CDEF be $S$. What is the length of AE when the area of rectangle CDEF is maximized? What is the maximum area?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given: $S_{\text{rectangle } CDEF} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}x^2 + 3\sqrt{3}x\ (0 < x < 12)$\\
$= -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(x^2 - 12x)$\\
$= -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(x^2 - 12x + 6^2 - 6^2)$\\
$= -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}[(x-6)^2 - 36]$\\
$= -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(x-6)^2 + 9\sqrt{3}$,\\
Therefore, when $x=\boxed{6}$, the area of rectangle CDEF is maximized,\\
meaning when point E is the midpoint of AB, the area of rectangle CDEF is maximized, with a maximum area of $\boxed{9\sqrt{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: [Image description] The figure is right triangle ABC: point C is at the lower left, AC is the vertical side going upward to A, CB is the horizontal side going rightward to B, and AB is the hypotenuse going from A down to the right to B; inside the triangle, a rectangle CDEF is cut out from C, the lower-left corner of the rectangle is at C, D is on AC (left boundary), F is on BC (bottom boundary), and E is on AB and is the upper-right corner of the rectangle; the upper side DE of the rectangle is a horizontal line, and the right side EF is a vertical line. [Coordinate-method reasoning] ∠C=90° and ∠A=30°, AB=12, so △ABC is a 30-60-90 triangle: BC(opposite 30°)=12/2=6, AC(opposite 60°)=6√3. Take coordinates C=(0,0), let AC be the y-axis and BC be the x-axis, then A=(0,6√3), B=(6,0). Point E is on AB and AE=x. Vector AB=B−A=(6,−6√3), |AB|=12, therefore the ratio from A to E is x/12: E = A + (x/12)·(6,−6√3) = (x/2, 6√3 − (√3/2)x). Since in the figure the sides of the rectangle are parallel to the coordinate axes, the rectangle width CF equals the x-coordinate of E, x_E=x/2, and the height CD equals the y-coordinate of E, y_E=6√3 − (√3/2)x. Therefore the area S(x) = (x/2)·(6√3 − (√3/2)x) = 3√3 x − (√3/4)x^2, (0<x<12). This is a quadratic function opening downward, and the maximum value is at the vertex: x = −b/(2a) = −(3√3)/(2·(−√3/4)) = 6. The maximum area S_max = S(6) = 3√3·6 − (√3/4)·36 = 18√3 − 9√3 = 9√3.
